scope.definition: Dependency and security maintenance is the closed loop from inventory and advisory/release detection through update proposal, security/code scan, compatibility validation, risk-aware approval/merge, deployment observation, rollback and exception aging. It covers manifest/lockfile updates, container/action/toolchain pins, SCA, SAST/secret/misconfiguration scans and machine- or AI-generated fixes. It does not claim full autonomous incident response or general feature development.
systems_in_scope: GitHub Dependabot alerts/version/security updates/dependency review and CodeQL Copilot Autofix
OSV-Scanner, Trivy, OpenSSF Scorecard, Sigstore/SLSA verification
commercial examples Snyk and Semgrep as optional scanners; detailed product claims are not relied on
scope.time_range: 2019 through 2026-09-13, with a 2017 automation experiment and 2018 event-stream incident as foundations.

current_state.claim: Bots can discover declared dependencies, query advisory/release metadata, edit supported manifests and lockfiles, open grouped PRs, rebase, and merge selected low-risk updates after repository-required checks. Dependabot configuration and Renovate document these controls.
PR-time dependency review can block newly introduced vulnerable/disallowed dependencies; CodeQL can propose fixes for supported alerts; OSV-Scanner and Trivy can produce CI-consumable findings.

No listed scanner or bot proves semantic compatibility, exploitability, maintainer trust, or absence of malicious code. GitHub explicitly says Autofix may be incorrect or insecure; the event-stream compromise shows a legitimate-looking dependency update can itself carry malicious code.

Safe auto-merge is mature for narrow, reversible, well-tested update classes. Autonomous merging of major versions, runtime-critical packages, unsigned/unprovenanced artifacts, workflow changes or generated security fixes remains conditional on human/security review.

GitHub documents a default three-day cooldown for Dependabot version updates (not security updates). Renovate warns that GitHub platform-native automerge can merge despite failing non-required checks and can ignore Renovate merge windows; required status checks and correct platformAutomerge policy are therefore mandatory.

representative_systems.name: Dependabot
representative_systems.role: GitHub-native advisory alerts plus version/security update PRs
representative_systems.strengths: Low setup friction, GitHub Advisory Database/dependency graph integration, repository rules and dependency review.
representative_systems.limits: Supported ecosystems/manifest resolution; GitHub-hosted control plane; PR Actions secrets/token restrictions; less policy flexibility than Renovate.

representative_systems.name: Renovate
representative_systems.role: Highly configurable multi-platform update orchestration, hosted or self-hosted
representative_systems.strengths: Package rules, grouping, dashboards, schedules, minimum release age, vulnerability-alert paths and automerge.
representative_systems.limits: Large policy surface; unsafe presets/regex/custom managers or overprivileged tokens can widen risk; requires operating discipline.

representative_systems.name: GitHub dependency review + CodeQL/Autofix
representative_systems.role: PR admission control and SAST remediation suggestions
representative_systems.strengths: Native status checks and review UI.
representative_systems.limits: Language/query coverage and generated-fix fallibility; not an approval oracle.

representative_systems.name: OSV-Scanner
representative_systems.role: Open-source SCA for lockfiles, SBOMs and source; machine-readable CI output
representative_systems.strengths: Open vulnerability schema/database integration and self-hosting.
representative_systems.limits: Only finds known, represented vulnerabilities and resolvable packages.

representative_systems.name: Trivy
representative_systems.strengths: Broad scan surface and CI integration.
representative_systems.limits: Scanner breadth does not remove triage, database freshness or false-positive/negative problems.

representative_systems.name: OpenSSF Scorecard + SLSA/Sigstore
representative_systems.role: Upstream hygiene signals and artifact provenance/signature policy
representative_systems.strengths: Adds supplier/build identity evidence that CVE-only scanning lacks.
representative_systems.limits: Score/rules are signals; signed provenance does not make code safe.

representative_systems.name: Snyk, Mend, Semgrep, Socket and ecosystem-native audit tools
representative_systems.role: Buy alternatives for SCA/SAST/reachability, remediation PRs and malicious-package signals
representative_systems.strengths: May add curated intelligence, reachability or support.
representative_systems.limits: Capabilities, pricing, telemetry and false-positive rates change; validate against the project’s own corpus.

primary_evidence.claim: Dependabot’s schema supports schedules, groups, cooldown, PR limits, private registries, ignore/allow and target-branch configuration.
Dependabot security updates attempt the smallest secure upgrade and depend on supported manifests/lockfiles and resolvability.

Renovate exposes automerge, grouping, stability delay/minimumReleaseAge, vulnerability alerts and internal checks; its own docs warn self-hosters about permissions and untrusted repository configuration.
Branch/ruleset protections supply required checks, reviews and constrained bypass independently of bot intent.
GitHub says CodeQL Autofix suggestions can be wrong, insecure, incomplete or behavior-changing and require review/testing.
SLSA verification evaluates provenance authenticity and expected builder/source identity; Sigstore verification must bind signature to an approved key or identity/issuer.
CISA KEV indicates observed exploitation; EPSS estimates 30-day exploitation probability. Neither represents application reachability or business impact.

independent_evidence.claim: A 2021 study of 2,904 JavaScript projects found 65.42% of Dependabot security PRs accepted, often in one day; 3.2% of manually inspected PRs had build breakage. Severity and breaking-change risk were not strongly tied to merge time. External validity is limited to sampled public JavaScript repositories and historical Dependabot behavior.

A 2024 large study analyzed 9,916,318 PR-related issues from 1,743,035 projects and reported Dependabot above 65% of dependency-management activity and sub-day handling after security PR creation, but average hidden-vulnerability and patch-disclosure delays of 512 and 362 days respectively. A bot accelerates the post-disclosure tail, not discovery.
A 2022 mixed-method study reported 77% of sampled projects tried more than one bot and identified notification/PR noise plus practice adaptation as adoption/removal factors.
The event-stream incident demonstrates that automatic consumption of a newly published release can import malicious code before conventional advisory controls catch it.

In 1,823 projects/540,665 Dependabot PRs, mean npm technical lag in a 613-project cohort fell 48.99 to 25.38 days 90 days after adoption (median 13.96 to 3.62); >70% PRs merged. Only 3.4% had a known compatibility score, noise controls were common and 11.3% of projects deprecated Dependabot. Adopters were already proactive, so causality/generalization is bounded.

A 2023 study of 4,195 closed security updates in 978 JavaScript projects found 57% PR merge; 53.48% of vulnerabilities fixed by bot, 30.27% manually and 16.25% unresolved. About half of bot fixes landed within one day, yet estimated probability of remaining unresolved after a year was 18%.

Across six SCA tools and 21,130 Maven modules, mean vulnerability-report F1 was .475; build scan dependency-detection F1 .890 versus .692 pre-build. Correct scan mode/method/scope reduced false positives and negatives.
Studies found malicious packages, source-untraceable release files and weak publisher/package signals at ecosystem scale. Passing CVE and CI checks therefore does not establish release trust.

reference_workflow.trigger: merge, scheduled daily scan, lockfile/SBOM change, new registry/advisory event
actions: Generate/refresh resolved dependency graph and SBOM including direct/transitive, dev/build, container base images, GitHub Actions and toolchains.
Record owner, runtime criticality, internet exposure, environment and current digest/version.
Run at least SCA plus secret, SAST and IaC/container scanners where relevant.
Deduplicate by package, advisory, path and fixed version. Preserve scanner provenance and timestamp.
Combine affected resolved path and runtime reachability with fix availability, KEV, EPSS, severity, asset exposure and business impact.
Critical/no-fix issues open an incident or compensating-control task; do not wait for the routine bot queue.
Bot chooses the minimum fixed version for vulnerabilities; routine updates follow semver and package rules.
Group only packages with the same lifecycle/blast radius; separate majors, runtime/security-critical and build/workflow changes.
Regenerate lockfiles in a hermetic ephemeral environment; attach changelog, dependency diff, advisory paths, provenance and risk rationale.
Reject unexpected registries, namespace changes, new install scripts/binaries/licenses or dependency confusion.
Enforce release-age soak for routine updates; bypass only for confirmed urgent patches after review.
Where supported, verify digest, signature and SLSA provenance against approved identities/builders. Pin CI actions by full SHA.

Run clean install with lockfile frozen; compile/type/lint/unit/integration/contract tests, package-specific smoke/regression tests, dependency review, SCA/SAST/secrets/IaC scans and license/policy checks.
Build once; test/promote the same immutable artifact. Compare behavior/performance and SBOM to baseline.
Generated security fixes receive targeted exploit regression tests where feasible.

Auto-merge only allowlisted patch/minor/dev dependency classes with no sensitive-file diff, trusted provenance, adequate tests, release-age/merge-confidence policy and zero unresolved high-risk findings.
Use platform rules/merge queue, never a bot-admin bypass. Majors, runtime-critical libraries, workflow/auth/crypto changes, new maintainers/packages and AI autofixes require owner/security approval.
outputs: merged, queued, escalated or rejected decision

actions: Deploy canary or low-risk cohort; watch errors, latency, security signals and business invariants.
Automatically pause/rollback on explicit thresholds; retain artifact and prior lockfile for fast rollback.
Close finding only after deployed inventory proves fixed version.
On failure, label root cause, suppress duplicate retry storms, tune tests/rules with reviewed change and expire exceptions.

integration_points.mechanics: GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket app or scoped token; PR comments/check runs, CODEOWNERS, rulesets, merge queue and audit log.
Ecosystem registries plus private-registry credentials; lockfiles and update APIs. Isolate read tokens from publishing credentials.
GitHub Advisory Database/OSV plus vendor feeds; enrich with CISA KEV and EPSS, asset/reachability context.
Status checks for tests/scans; ephemeral runners; cache isolation; SBOM, attestations, OCI registry and immutable digest promotion. Dependabot-triggered Actions have distinct token/secret behavior.
Issue/SIEM/on-call routing for SLA breaches; deployment controller and observability for canary/rollback; exception registry with expiry and owner; metrics warehouse for PR-to-deploy lifecycle.

human_gates.when: initial rollout and every material rule/scanner/permission change
human_gates.why: Humans define risk appetite, update classes, test sufficiency, trusted builders/registries and rollback thresholds.

human_gates.when: major version; runtime-critical/auth/crypto/database/network package; workflow/installer/build script; new package/maintainer/registry; broad transitive churn
human_gates.why: Semver/checks cannot establish semantic or supplier trust.

human_gates.when: CodeQL/AI/autofix changes logic or lacks a reproducing security test
human_gates.why: Vendor documentation explicitly denies correctness/security guarantees.

human_gates.when: no fix, unresolvable graph, check disagreement, required secret unavailable, fix violates compatibility, SLA breach or proposed bypass
human_gates.why: Requires product tradeoff, compensating control or accepted risk with owner and expiry.

human_gates.when: canary threshold fires or rollback fails
human_gates.why: Contain impact and choose forward-fix versus rollback.

failure_modes.detail: Undeclared/dynamic/vendored dependencies, missing lockfiles, unsupported ecosystems, stale advisory databases and alias/version mismatch cause false negatives; scanners generally cannot find undisclosed vulnerabilities.
Weak/flaky tests and build-only checks miss API, behavioral, data, performance and security regressions. The 2021 3.2% build-break figure is not a semantic-correctness rate.
A newest or CVE-free release may be malicious; install scripts and CI workflows can exfiltrate secrets. Release-age delay helps for routine releases but conflicts with urgent patching.
Overbroad app/token rights, untrusted repository config, pull_request_target misuse, mutable action tags and secret-bearing reruns let changed code reach credentials.
Required checks evaluated on stale heads, concurrent updates, merge-train interactions, misconfigured branch rules or admin bypass can merge an untested combination.
Update floods consume review/CI, collide with each other, go stale and train maintainers to ignore security alerts.

No fixed release, incompatible constraints, abandoned package, vulnerable transitive dependency or broken lockfile prevents an automatic PR. Vendoring/forking/replacement or compensating control is a human architecture decision.
SAST/AI suggestion can be incorrect, incomplete or introduce another vulnerability.
CVSS alone overprioritizes unreachable code and underrepresents active exploitation/business context; KEV/EPSS also have bounded meanings.
Excess CI, proprietary-seat/scan cost, rate limits and unclear ownership can make apparently free automation costly; bot acceptance metrics do not show deployment success or maintenance burden.
A scanner report may look green to CI because its process exits successfully despite findings. Trivy explicitly exits 0 by default; GitHub/Snyk findings block only when checks/rules are required.

failure_modes.mode: Remediation tool executes untrusted project hooks
failure_modes.detail: OSV-Scanner guided remediation can invoke package-manager behavior, scripts or project-specified registries. Running autofix with secrets or unrestricted network can turn repair into code execution/exfiltration.

mechanics: Read-only discovery token; separate narrowly scoped PR-write identity; no package publish/cloud-deploy rights.
Ephemeral network-restricted update/test runner; Dependabot secrets separate from Actions secrets; never execute unreviewed fork/bot code with write token.
Pin actions to full SHA and protect workflow/config files with CODEOWNERS.
Ruleset requires fresh status checks on current head, review for sensitive paths, conversation resolution and merge queue.
Bot cannot bypass or alter its own policy/check workflow. Break-glass is named, logged and reviewed.
Allowlist ecosystems/update types; conservative PR concurrency; dashboard/group only compatible same-owner packages; stagger schedules.
Use minimumReleaseAge for routine releases, but an explicit reviewed emergency lane for exploited vulnerabilities.
Frozen clean install, multi-layer tests, dependency diff/review, SCA/SAST/secret/IaC/license gates.
Provenance/signature/registry policy and immutable artifact promotion. A second scanner can detect coverage differences but correlated databases mean it is not automatically independent.
Canary, automated threshold rollback, prior artifact/lockfile retention and kill switch.
Close vulnerabilities on deployed evidence; quarantine bad versions; cap retries and CI spend.
Dismissal needs reason, owner, compensating control and expiry; recurring review reopens stale risk.
Log bot version/config, advisory snapshot, inputs, diffs, checks, approvals, artifact digest, deployment and rollback.

controls_and_mitigations.control: Make findings enforcing and record the baseline
mechanics: Set scanner nonzero exit policy and severity/reachability thresholds explicitly; protect that status check.
Understand delta semantics: a passing before/after PR check can still leave baseline vulnerabilities. Record database/tool versions and re-scan the built artifact.

production_ready: Inventory for supported ecosystems; scheduled update PR generation; advisory matching; routine SCA/SAST/secret/IaC checks; protected-branch merge after deterministic CI; dashboards and audit trails.
conditionally_useful: Auto-merge for narrowly allowlisted patch/minor/dev updates with strong tests, trusted suppliers, release soak and rapid rollback; automated security-patch PRs; CodeQL/AI autofix as a reviewed draft.
emerging_or_weak: Accurate reachability across languages, malicious-package detection, fully automatic major migrations, general semantic patch validation, autonomous no-fix mitigation and risk scoring that transfers between projects.
maturity_assessment.rationale: Independent studies show substantial PR acceptance and fast post-PR remediation, yet also noise, bot switching and long pre-disclosure delay. Official Autofix limitations and supply-chain incidents rule out treating green scanners as proof.

build_vs_buy.buy_or_managed: Use Dependabot when GitHub-native coverage and low operations burden dominate. Consider managed Renovate/Mend, Snyk, Semgrep or similar where policy support, curated intelligence, reachability and support justify cost. Validate claims in a shadow trial.
build_vs_buy.self_host_or_open: Self-host Renovate for cross-platform/deep policy and OSV-Scanner/Trivy/Scorecard for transparent CI, accepting upgrades, database mirrors, credentials, queues and availability as your responsibility.
custom_engineering_needed: risk normalization across feeds and duplicate advisories
end-to-end metrics from alert through deployed fix
build_vs_buy.selection_test: Run 30–60 days in report-only/shadow mode on historical known incidents and current manifests. Compare supported dependency coverage, true/false triage load, fixability, PR conflict/noise, CI cost, time-to-deployed-fix, permissions/data residency and exportability. Do not select on alert count.

recommended_pattern.routine_lane: Renovate or Dependabot batches allowlisted patch/minor/dev updates on a fixed cadence. Apply 3–7 day release soak (project-specific), strict PR/CI budgets, immutable inputs and auto-merge only after full checks through the normal merge queue. Majors and sensitive diffs stay manual.
recommended_pattern.security_lane: Continuously reconcile inventory against GitHub Advisory/OSV and vendor data; prioritize with affected path/reachability, KEV, EPSS, exposure and impact. Open the minimum-fix PR immediately. Confirmed exploited/reachable issues bypass routine soak only with owner/security approval, focused regression test and canary.
merge_predicate: bot identity and config are approved
diff is within update-class and sensitive-path policy
registry/publisher/digest and, where available, signature/provenance satisfy policy
no new disallowed license, install script, secret or high-risk dependency
all required fresh checks pass on current merge candidate
release-age or reviewed emergency exception satisfied
rollback artifact and observation rule exist
rollout: Phase 1 bot PRs with manual merge; measure coverage, noise, false findings and regressions.
Phase 2 auto-merge dev and low-risk patch updates behind ruleset and canary.
Phase 3 expand package-by-package only from measured evidence; keep major/sensitive/generated-fix gates.
recommended_pattern.why: This captures the demonstrated speed advantage without granting scanners/bots authority they cannot justify.

open_questions.question: What fraction of the project’s resolved runtime/build/container/action graph is actually detected by each scanner?
open_questions.evidence_needed: Golden SBOM plus seeded vulnerable, aliased, vendored and private packages by ecosystem.

open_questions.question: Which dependency changes are semantically covered by tests?
open_questions.evidence_needed: Mutation/contract tests, historical update failures and canary outcome linked to package/update class.

open_questions.question: How accurate are reachability, malicious-package and AI-autofix claims on this repository?
open_questions.evidence_needed: Blind project-specific benchmark with labeled findings/fixes; vendors rarely publish transferable false-negative rates.

open_questions.question: What release-age window best trades zero-day supply-chain exposure against patch latency?
open_questions.evidence_needed: Registry/ecosystem incident base rates, criticality and emergency override data; no universal threshold.

open_questions.question: How should coordinated multi-package or major migrations be automated safely?
open_questions.evidence_needed: Repository-specific integration/e2e coverage and atomic rollout/rollback design.

open_questions.question: Do empirical GitHub public-project results transfer to private monorepos and deployment outcomes?
open_questions.evidence_needed: Private operational cohorts tracking merged-to-deployed success, incidents, reviewer time and full cost.

open_questions.question: What post-2026-09-13 changes occurred?
open_questions.evidence_needed: Future changelogs and new independent studies; outside this snapshot.

supported_claims: Generated security fixes have coverage and correctness limitations including semantic changes, new vulnerabilities and unsafe dependency/version suggestions.

sources.title: Dependabot errors
supported_claims: Security/update jobs can fail due to unresolvable constraints, inaccessible registries, credential/certificate issues, resolution errors or hosted-job timeout.

sources.title: Automatic Fix PR rules
supported_claims: Snyk automatic fix PRs follow recurring retests, thresholds and grouping; a fix may introduce other vulnerabilities and is selected by relative severity policy.

sources.title: Pull request checks
supported_claims: Snyk PR checks compare before/after and only enforce merge when made required by repository branch protection; a pass does not certify a clean baseline.

sources.title: Autofix for Semgrep Code
supported_claims: Semgrep AI Autofix opens a draft PR and requires repository write permission; humans retain review/merge responsibility.

sources.title: Rule-defined autofix
supported_claims: Semgrep rules can define deterministic fix templates and preview/apply them; semantic correctness still needs project validation.

sources.title: Guided remediation
supported_claims: Experimental fix strategies edit npm/Maven manifests or lockfiles; users must reinstall/test, and untrusted projects can cause package-manager scripts or external registries to execute.

sources.title: Vulnerability scanning
supported_claims: Trivy’s vendor advisory and detection-mode choices trade false positives and false negatives; unsupported/self-compiled packages and unspecified ranges can limit detection.

sources.title: Exit code
supported_claims: Trivy returns exit code 0 by default even when findings exist; enforcing CI must set --exit-code and policy.

confidence.overall: High for documented mechanics and controls; moderate for general operational effectiveness; low-to-moderate for cross-project false-negative rates and malicious-package/autofix accuracy.
high: reported sample sizes and outcomes in cited papers
moderate: Generalization that narrow auto-merge is safe when the stated gates hold
recommended SLOs and release-soak durations, which are engineering judgments
low_or_unknown: Vendor-comparative accuracy and total cost without a project trial
confidence.reason: Primary documentation establishes capabilities, three peer-reviewed studies provide independent operational evidence, but most docs are continuously updated and tool efficacy depends strongly on ecosystem, tests, policy and repository context.

conflicts.conflict: Fast fixes versus slow vulnerability lifecycle
conflicts.evidence: Studies report many security PRs merged within a day, but the 2024 study reports vulnerabilities hidden 512 days and patch disclosure after 362 days on average.
conflicts.resolution: The clocks measure different stages. Automation shortens detection-to-PR/PR-to-merge after a machine-readable fix exists; it does not discover unknown flaws.

conflicts.conflict: Low observed build breakage versus unsafe-autofix warning
conflicts.evidence: The 2021 Dependabot study observed 3.2% build breakage in a manual subsample; GitHub states CodeQL Autofix can be wrong or insecure.
conflicts.resolution: Dependency version PRs and generated source-code security fixes differ, and build success is weaker than semantic/security correctness. Both can be true.

conflicts.conflict: Release delay versus emergency patch speed
conflicts.evidence: Renovate stability delay reduces exposure to freshly compromised releases/noise, while KEV and fast-remediation practice favor immediate fixes.
conflicts.resolution: Use separate routine and confirmed-exploited lanes, with a reviewed bypass and canary rather than one global delay.

conflicts.evidence: OSV/Trivy/GitHub feeds can overlap and share upstream advisories.
conflicts.resolution: Use multiple tools for complementary ecosystem/surface coverage, not a majority vote; measure unique finds and correlated gaps.

conflicts.evidence: Dependabot exceeded 65% of activity in the 2024 study, while 77% of projects in the 2022 study tried multiple bots.
conflicts.resolution: Popularity reflects accessibility/integration, not universal fit; policy flexibility and noise explain switching.

conflicts.conflict: Security-PR acceptance and severity effects differ by study
conflicts.evidence: 2021 reported 65.42% acceptance and severity not strongly tied to merge time; 2023 reported 57% merge and low-severity vulnerabilities 2.3× likelier than critical to persist after a year.
conflicts.resolution: Different Dependabot generations, periods, samples and unit/lifecycle methods; preserve both rather than average.

conflicts.conflict: GitHub documentation appears inconsistent on security-update PR limits
conflicts.evidence: The 2026 Dependabot options reference states security PRs do not count toward the version-update limit and describes no cap, while the security-update concepts/reference material reports a limit of 10.
conflicts.resolution: Treat the effective cap as version/account/feature dependent and verify in the target repository/API before relying on concurrency behavior.

uncertain: Exact current commercial packaging, prices and proprietary detection accuracy for Snyk, Mend, Semgrep and Socket were not independently verified and are intentionally excluded from comparative claims.
No source provides a universal false-positive/false-negative or regression rate across ecosystems; project-specific shadow evaluation is required.
Several continuously maintained documentation pages do not expose a stable publication/update date. Their access date and URL are recorded.
Release-soak windows and suggested SLOs are recommendations, not evidence-backed universal constants.
GitHub’s 2026 documentation is inconsistent about whether Dependabot security-update PRs have no cap or a limit of 10; verify behavior in the target repository.
